headline: Record revenue, margin gains — but profit outlook trimmed
summary_short: Southwest posted record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $8.43 billion (+16.4% y/y) and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.47 (+20.5% y/y), but cut full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.25-$4.25 from its prior 'at least $4.00' outlook.
summary_long: Record Q2 revenue of $8.43B (+16.4% y/y) was driven by managed-business growth (+30% y/y), Rapid Rewards momentum, and Chase co-brand card gains, plus a $285M one-time breakage-revenue reversal. Operating income rose 26.7% y/y to $285M and adjusted operating margin expanded 3.3pts to 6.7% despite an $889M y/y jump in fuel expense, as non-fuel unit costs (CASM-X +3.4%) came in below guidance. Net income rose 9.4% to $233M; diluted EPS rose faster (+20.5%) on an 8.9% y/y reduction in weighted diluted shares. Cash stood at $3.79B, up from $3.33B at Q1-end. The company cut full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4.00' and trimmed capacity growth guidance to ~1.5% from 2%.

drivers.explanation: Managed business revenue rose 30% y/y and Chase co-brand card acquisitions rose 28% y/y; results also include a $285M breakage-revenue reversal (special item) from revised flight-credit redemption assumptions.
Adjusted operating margin expanded 3.3pts despite an $889M y/y fuel-expense increase, as non-fuel unit costs (CASM-X +3.4%) rose less than prior guidance called for.
EPS growth (+20.5% y/y) outpaced net income growth (+9.4% y/y) because weighted diluted shares fell 8.9% y/y on buybacks executed in prior periods.
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was cut to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4.00', and capacity growth guidance was lowered to about 1.5% from 2%, both citing the fuel-cost environment.
